transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-29
Time: 15:00 PDT
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Emma Carter (Redwood AE), Sanjay Patel (Redwood SE), Maya Thompson (CISO, Lake District Health), Carlos Rivera (Head of Infra), Priya Singh (Data Privacy Lead)

Summary (auto):
High-level security review focusing on data handling and privacy: prompt retention, PHI/PII controls, encryption/KMS options, SOC 2/ISO artifacts, RBAC/SSO, audit logs. Customer requested written confirmation on model training policy (no training on customer data) and options for Private/VPC or on-prem deployment for PHI use cases.

Topics:
- SOC 2 / ISO artifacts and attestation
- Data retention and prompt/content deletion
- PHI handling, HIPAA implications
- Encryption at rest / customer-managed KMS/HSM
- RBAC and SSO (SAML / OIDC)
- Audit logs and access controls
- Private deployment / VPC / on-prem options

Transcript:
[00:00:05] Emma Carter: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, this is Emma from Redwood, with Sanjay on the line. We're excited to walk through security and privacy details for Lake District Health.
[00:00:14] Maya Thompson: Thanks, Emma. Quick note, I'm Maya, CISO. We handle PHI, so primary concerns are data residency, no inadvertent model training, and auditability.
[00:00:27] Carlos Rivera: Carlos here, infra. We'll dig into networking and KMS details.
[00:00:33] Priya Singh: And I'm Priya on privacy, looking at retention policies and consent flows.
[00:00:40] Sanjay Patel: Great, high level first: Redwood supports Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments. For PHI workloads we typically recommend Private (VPC) or on-prem. We'll outline the differences.
[00:00:52] Maya Thompson: On-hosted: can you confirm whether data is used for model training? We need a written statement.
[00:01:00] Emma Carter: Short answer: Redwood does not train customer-provided data into our models. I'll capture that in writing after the call; Sanjay can also explain isolation controls.
[00:01:12] Sanjay Patel: Right. We have a formal non-training policy for customer content. For hosted tenants we keep logs for observability but they are not fed back into model training. For Private and Dedicated, customer data never leaves their VPC unless explicitly configured.
[00:01:28] Priya Singh: How long are prompts and responses retained by default on Hosted?
[00:01:33] Sanjay Patel: Default retention is 30 days for Hosted audit/ops logs, but retention windows are configurable—30, 90, or customizable per contract for Dedicated/Private. We can also support immediate purge APIs for transcripts.
[00:01:48] Maya Thompson: Do you offer an API to purge prompt history and confirm deletion? We need a paper trail for audits.
[00:01:55] Emma Carter: Yes, we provide a deletion API and will include log entries showing deletion events; we also produce audit export that shows who requested deletion and when.
[00:02:06] Carlos Rivera: For encryption: we want CMK (customer-managed key) support. Can Redwood use our KMS?
[00:02:12] Sanjay Patel: Yes, we support customer-managed KMS integrations. For Hosted we integrate with cloud KMS providers—AWS KMS, GCP KMS—via an encrypted key wrap protocol; for Private/on-prem we support direct HSM integrations. We'll share the KMS integration guide.
[00:02:28] Maya Thompson: Is data encrypted in transit and at rest?
[00:02:32] Sanjay Patel: Yes. TLS 1.2+ in transit, and AES-256 at rest. With CMK you control the envelope key and can rotate or revoke.
[00:02:40] Priya Singh: About PHI — are there any model components that might inadvertently log sensitive fields? Examples: we send KV cache to GPUs for inference, could that leak?
[00:02:52] Sanjay Patel: Good question. We manage KV cache in memory on the serving pods only; it's not written to persistent storage unless the customer opts into caching for performance. For PHI-sensitive workloads we recommend disabling persistent caching and using Private mode. Note: transcript may transcribe as "K V cash" sometimes in logs.
[00:03:06] Maya Thompson: Okay. We also need RBAC and SSO — we'll need SCIM provisioning and SAML.
[00:03:12] Emma Carter: We support SAML and OIDC SSO, SCIM for user provisioning, and role-based access controls with audit trails. Roles are customizable; typical roles: admin, developer, auditor, read-only.
[00:03:25] Carlos Rivera: Can audit logs capture token-level access and model route used?
[00:03:31] Sanjay Patel: Yes, audit logs capture request metadata: requestor ID, route/model, timestamp, token ID, IP (if enabled), and response status. We can also stream logs to your SIEM (Splunk/Datadog) or push to S3 with lifecycle rules.
[00:03:46] Priya Singh: For HIPAA compliance, do you sign BAAs?
[00:03:50] Emma Carter: We do sign BAAs for eligible plans and enterprise customers. That falls under our Private/Dedicated enterprise offering. We'll have legal follow up on exact BAA terms.
[00:03:59] Maya Thompson: Need to confirm physical data residency — can we pin to US-East or a single-region deployment?
[00:04:05] Sanjay Patel: Yes, region pinning is supported on Dedicated and Private. Hosted can be pinned to region where we have capacity; we'll note region constraints in the contract.
[00:04:15] Maya Thompson: Good. A few more items: Do you maintain SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 artifacts?
[00:04:22] Emma Carter: We have SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001; I'll send the reports and a summary.
[00:04:27] Carlos Rivera: Network setup for Private: can we bring our own peering and IP allowlist?
[00:04:33] Sanjay Patel: Yes, Private supports VPC peering, transit gateways, and customer-controlled IP allowlists. We'll include network diagrams.
[00:04:41] Priya Singh: About data minimization: can we configure to not store prompts at all, only ephemeral processing?
[00:04:47] Sanjay Patel: For Dedicated/Private you can set processing-only mode where we do not persist prompts. For Hosted, ephemeral mode is possible but limited by features that require logs (e.g., usage analytics). We'll document tradeoffs.
[00:04:58] Maya Thompson: For legal, we need a written 'no training' attestation specifying that Redwood or its partners won't train models on our data without explicit consent.
[00:05:06] Emma Carter: We'll provide an attestation letter. To be clear: Redwood's policy is we do not use customer content to train our base models. Any research usage is scoped and requires explicit customer opt-in in writing.
[00:05:17] Maya Thompson: Great. On the auditability side, if a user requests deletion under GDPR, will you show us the deletion logs?
[00:05:24] Sanjay Patel: Yes, deletion logs include requestor, resource IDs, and timestamps; we can provide exports for compliance purposes.
[00:05:31] Carlos Rivera: Operationally, we want SIEM integration. Which outputs?
[00:05:35] Sanjay Patel: We support syslog, Kafka, HTTP webhooks, S3 exports, and direct Splunk forwarder.
[00:05:42] Priya Singh: How do you isolate multi-tenant metadata? E.g., model catalog info, model variants available per tenant?
[00:05:48] Emma Carter: Model catalog is tenant-aware; metadata is per-tenant. Model weights are either shared (for open models) or can be provisioned per-tenant in Dedicated/Private.
[00:05:58] Maya Thompson: For the pilot we might start with non-PHI data on Hosted, then move to Private for PHI. Timeline asks: can you support a pilot in April?
[00:06:06] Emma Carter: Yes, timeline seems doable. We'll follow up with the SOC/ISO docs and a proposed pilot scope.
[00:06:12] Maya Thompson: Any third parties involved in processing? Subprocessors?
[00:06:16] Emma Carter: We maintain a subprocessors list; typical cloud infra providers are listed. We'll share the latest subprocessors list and compliance attestations.
[00:06:25] Carlos Rivera: Encryption key rotation — if we rotate in KMS, how quickly does Redwood pick up the new key?
[00:06:31] Sanjay Patel: For envelope keys, rotation is immediate on next API call after key propagation. For long-lived sessions we recommend a short key TTL; we'll include recommendations.
[00:06:42] Priya Singh: About data classification: can we tag data flows as PHI so certain controls apply?
[00:06:46] Sanjay Patel: Yes, Redwood supports metadata tagging on requests; policies can change retention and logging behavior when PHI tag is present.
[00:06:55] Maya Thompson: We need to confirm where embeddings are stored; are they subject to the same retention and encryption?
[00:07:01] Sanjay Patel: Embeddings are stored in your chosen vector store; Redwood can host or you can bring your own. If we host embeddings for you, they inherit the same retention settings and CMK.
[00:07:12] Emma Carter: Quick note: sometimes transcript says 'KV cache' as 'K V cash' — just FYI in auto-transcription.
[00:07:18] Priya Singh: Do you have an incident response plan and notification SLA?
[00:07:22] Emma Carter: Yes: we have incident classification, 24/7 on-call, and notification SLAs based on severity. We'll share the incident response playbook.
[00:07:31] Maya Thompson: Ok, security okays but legal will want the BAA and privacy addendum.
[00:07:36] Emma Carter: We'll kick off legal conversation after we share docs.
[00:07:40] Carlos Rivera: One more question — are there any known limitations with HIPAA-scope logs in Hosted?
[00:07:46] Sanjay Patel: Hosted can be configured to meet many controls, but for full HIPAA support we usually recommend Dedicated or Private with BAA. Hosted plus BAA is possible for certain customers, we'll check with legal.
[00:07:58] Maya Thompson: If Redwood provides a 'no training' attestation, do you also commit to not deriving fine-tuned customer models behind the scenes?
[00:08:05] Emma Carter: We will include explicit language: no training, fine-tuning, or model weight updates using customer data without explicit written consent.
[00:08:12] Priya Singh: Can we get a sample data processing addendum (DPA)?
[00:08:16] Emma Carter: Yes, we'll send a DPA template.
[00:08:20] Maya Thompson: Ok thanks.
[00:08:22] [--- several minutes of clarifying questions, details omitted for brevity ---]
[00:18:45] Sanjay Patel: Diving a bit deeper on Private deployment: network egress is controlled by the customer's VPC, logs can be routed to your S3 bucket, and we support in-line IP allowlists. For on-prem we provide an appliance image.
[00:19:02] Carlos Rivera: For the appliance, what's the HA story?
[00:19:06] Sanjay Patel: Appliance supports active/standby with failover, and we document recommended specs. We'll include the HA doc in the follow-up.
[00:19:16] Priya Singh: For consent capture, where do you surface data subject requests?
[00:19:20] Emma Carter: We have an admin UI for data subject request exports and a DSR API.
[00:19:26] Maya Thompson: How do you manage developer tokens? We need token scoping and expiry.
[00:19:31] Sanjay Patel: Tokens can be short-lived, scoped to routes, and you can revoke them via API. We also provide org-level token policies.
[00:19:38] Carlos Rivera: Logging retention for audit: what's the maximum retention you support?
[00:19:42] Sanjay Patel: We can support multi-year retention in Dedicated/Private; Hosted has limits but can be extended via archiving to your storage.
[00:19:50] Emma Carter: Recap — action items I'll capture.
[00:19:54] Maya Thompson: Good.
[00:20:00] [Noise, brief hold music as someone checks docs]
[00:25:12] Emma Carter: Quick recap before we close: we'll send SOC 2 and ISO docs, subprocessors list, KMS integration guide, BAA template and DPA, and a short attestation on 'no training on customer data'. We'll also send network diagrams for Private and the deletion API spec.
[00:25:33] Priya Singh: Please include the API endpoints and example deletion logs. That's critical.
[00:25:38] Sanjay Patel: Will do.
[00:25:41] Maya Thompson: And please note our pilot scope: start with non-PHI on Hosted in April, move PHI workloads to Private in May, legal to review BAA and DPA.
[00:25:51] Emma Carter: Noted — we'll propose dates in the follow-up.
[00:25:55] Carlos Rivera: Any blockers on our side? We'll gather the list of PHI endpoints and share with Emma and Sanjay.
[00:26:02] Maya Thompson: We'll also need a preliminary security questionnaire answered — our procurement needs it.
[00:26:08] Emma Carter: We'll fill out the questionnaire and return it within 3 business days.
[00:26:14] Priya Singh: Thanks. That covers most of it.
[00:26:18] Emma Carter: Great, thanks all. We'll follow up via email with the documents and set the demo for Private networking.
[00:26:25] Meeting end.
